project.name: jini
project.description: A reusable, product-neutral engine for running coding agents, exposing tools and providers, and streaming durable run events over HTTP, CLI, MCP, and sidecar transports. Extracted from Open Design; engine code under packages/ stays free of product-specific behavior.

nodes.name: StorageError

nodes.name: download.ts

nodes.languageNotes: 1095-line module with 55 internal functions implementing a complete download lifecycle including lock acquisition, resume logic, hash verification, and garbage collection.

nodes.name: ManagedDownloadError
nodes.summary: Custom error class for managed download failures with a typed error code and optional details payload.

nodes.name: normalizeChecksum
nodes.summary: Normalizes a caller-supplied checksum spec (algorithm + expected digest) into canonical form for manifest comparison.

nodes.name: normalizeSegment
nodes.summary: Validates and normalizes a single path segment used to build the managed download's on-disk target directory.

nodes.name: normalizeUrl
nodes.summary: Validates and normalizes the source URL for a managed download.

nodes.name: targetFromOptions
nodes.summary: Resolves a managed-download request's options into a concrete on-disk target (base path, containment check, url, checksum).

nodes.name: resetOwnedBase
nodes.summary: Clears and recreates a managed-download base directory that this process owns, guarding against resetting a directory it doesn't.

nodes.name: ensureManagedBase
nodes.summary: Ensures the managed-download base directory exists and is marked as owned by this store (writing/checking the sentinel file), resetting it if ownership is ambiguous.

nodes.name: isManifest
nodes.summary: Type-guard validating that a parsed JSON value has the shape of a download manifest.

nodes.name: lockBelongsToCurrentProcess
nodes.summary: Checks whether a persisted download lock file was written by this same process (pid + start-time match), distinguishing stale locks from active ones.

nodes.name: manifestMatchesTarget
nodes.summary: Compares a loaded manifest's url/checksum/basePath against the current target to decide whether previously-downloaded state can be reused.

nodes.name: createManifest
nodes.summary: Builds a new download manifest recording target, state, and an optional patch of additional fields.

nodes.name: parseContentRange
nodes.summary: Parses an HTTP Content-Range response header into start/end/total byte offsets for resumed downloads.

nodes.name: writeResponseBodyToPartial
nodes.summary: Streams a fetch Response body into the on-disk `.partial` file, reporting progress via the emit callback as bytes arrive.

nodes.name: tryResumeDownload
nodes.summary: Attempts to resume an interrupted download via an HTTP Range request against the previously-recorded byte offset and validators, falling back to a full re-download when the server's validators no longer match.

nodes.name: downloadFromZero
nodes.summary: Performs a full (non-resumed) download of the target URL into the partial file.

nodes.name: downloadWithRetries
nodes.summary: Runs a managed download attempt with retry/backoff, choosing between tryResumeDownload and downloadFromZero based on existing partial state.

nodes.name: acquireLock
nodes.summary: Acquires the per-target download lock file, detecting and clearing stale locks left by dead processes before writing a fresh one.

nodes.name: loadReusableState
nodes.summary: Loads any existing manifest/partial-file state for a target and determines how much of it can be reused for the current download request.

nodes.name: runManagedDownload
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a single managed-download run end to end: acquire lock, load reusable state, download with retries, persist the final manifest, and release the lock.

nodes.name: waitForTask
nodes.summary: Waits for an in-flight managed-download task to settle, optionally applying a timeout, for callers piggybacking on an already-running download.

nodes.name: managedDownload
nodes.summary: Public entry point that coordinates deduplication of in-flight downloads, locks, and progress listeners before delegating to the internal download pipeline.

nodes.name: requestClearAfterCopy
nodes.summary: Marks a completed managed download for clearing once its copy-and-clear consumer has finished reading it.

nodes.name: releaseCopyLease
nodes.summary: Releases a copy-and-clear lease on a managed download, removing the store's on-disk state if a clear was requested while the lease was held.

nodes.name: downloadCopyAndClear
nodes.summary: Downloads a file, atomically copies it to an output path, then removes the managed download store entry, supporting lease-based concurrency control.

nodes.name: inspectManagedDownload
nodes.summary: Reports the current manifest/lock/progress state of a managed download target without starting a new download.

nodes.name: removeManagedDownload
nodes.summary: Removes a managed download's on-disk manifest, partial file, and lock for a given target.

nodes.name: removeEntriesOlderThan
nodes.summary: Recursively removes managed-download entries under a root directory whose recorded age exceeds a cutoff.

nodes.name: pruneManagedDownloads
nodes.summary: Scans the managed-download store and removes entries older than a configured retention window.

nodes.name: pathContains

nodes.name: atomicCopyFile
nodes.summary: Copies a file atomically using a temp-file-then-rename strategy, with destination existence checks and cleanup on failure.

nodes.name: removePathBestEffort
nodes.summary: Removes a file or directory recursively, swallowing (not throwing on) errors so cleanup code can't itself fail a caller's operation.

nodes.name: readLogTail

nodes.name: resolveProjectRelativePath

nodes.name: createProcessStampArgs

nodes.name: readFlagValue

nodes.name: readProcessStamp

nodes.summary: Checks whether a decoded stamp matches a set of match criteria for a given contract.

nodes.summary: Checks whether a listed process snapshot's command line matches the given stamp criteria.

nodes.name: spawnLoggedProcess
nodes.summary: Spawns a process with stdout/stderr redirected to a log file descriptor.

nodes.name: isProcessAlive
nodes.summary: Checks whether a process with the given pid is currently alive.

nodes.name: waitForProcessExit
nodes.summary: Polls until a process with the given pid exits or a timeout elapses.

nodes.name: writeAntigravityModelSelection
nodes.summary: Persists a model selection label into Antigravity's settings.json file, creating the directory and file if necessary, and preserving existing settings fields.

nodes.name: acquireAntigravityModelLock

nodes.name: waitForAgyToReadModel
nodes.summary: Polls Antigravity's log file until a pattern matching the expected model selection appears, with configurable timeout and abort signal support.

nodes.name: codebuddy.ts

nodes.name: codexNeedsDangerFullAccessSandbox

nodes.name: copilot.ts

nodes.name: cursor-agent.ts

nodes.name: parseCursorAgentModels

nodes.name: deepseek.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the DeepSeek coding-agent CLI, specifying binary detection, static model options, and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: devin.ts

nodes.name: grok-build.ts

nodes.name: parseGrokBuildModels

nodes.name: hermes.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Hermes coding-agent CLI, specifying binary detection, model options, and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: index.ts

nodes.name: kilo.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Kilo coding-agent CLI, defining binary detection and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: kimi.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Kimi coding-agent CLI, specifying binary detection, model options, and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: kiro.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Kiro coding-agent CLI, defining binary detection and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: mimo.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Mimo coding-agent CLI, specifying binary detection, model options, and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: opencode.ts
nodes.summary: RuntimeAgentDef for the OpenCode CLI coding agent, with capability-flag support and model detection via line-separated parsing of stdout.

nodes.name: pi.ts
nodes.summary: RuntimeAgentDef for the Pi coding-agent CLI, defining binary detection, pi-rpc model probe, and detailed invocation arguments for print-mode operation.

nodes.name: qoder.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Qoder coding-agent CLI, specifying binary detection, model options, and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: qwen.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Qwen coding-agent CLI, defining binary detection and model options.

nodes.name: reasonix.ts
nodes.summary: RuntimeAgentDef for the Reasonix coding-agent CLI with a platform-aware helper that resolves the Reasonix home directory across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

nodes.name: shared.ts
nodes.summary: Shared helpers for per-CLI agent definitions: re-exports detectAcpModels, parsePiModels, execAgentFile, DEFAULT_MODEL_OPTION, and provides clampCodexReasoning (maps reasoning-effort levels to Codex-compatible values) and parseLineSeparatedModels (generic stdout model parser).

nodes.name: clampCodexReasoning
nodes.summary: Clamps reasoning-effort strings to values supported by specific GPT-5.x model variants, mapping unsupported levels to the nearest valid tier.

nodes.name: parseLineSeparatedModels
nodes.summary: Parses one-id-per-line CLI stdout into a deduplicated array of RuntimeModelOption objects, prepending the synthetic default model option.

nodes.name: trae-cli.ts
nodes.summary: Declarative RuntimeAgentDef for the Trae CLI coding agent, defining binary detection and invocation arguments.

nodes.name: launch.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves agent launch configuration including the executable path, detects Codex native binaries vs Node wrappers, and constructs the PATH env with toolchain and node_modules bin dirs.

nodes.name: resolveAgentLaunch
nodes.summary: Resolves the full launch descriptor for an agent: executable path, working directory, whether it is a native binary or Node wrapper.

nodes.name: applyAgentLaunchEnv
nodes.summary: Applies launch-specific environment modifications: prepends agent bin dir and toolchain dirs to PATH, deduplicates entries.

nodes.name: looksLikeCodexNodeWrapper
nodes.summary: Heuristically checks whether a resolved binary is a Node.js wrapper script (not a native binary) by reading its first bytes.

nodes.name: mcp.ts
nodes.summary: Constructs ACP MCP server input objects for a given agent, mapping the agent definition's MCP server descriptors into the format expected by session initialization.

nodes.name: buildAcpMcpServersForAgent
nodes.summary: Builds an array of AcpMcpServerInput from an agent definition and its session spec, merging server commands with environment variables.

nodes.name: metadata.ts
nodes.summary: Maintains install metadata (download URLs, documentation links) for known agents, used in diagnostic messages to guide users toward installation.

nodes.name: installMetaForAgent
nodes.summary: Looks up install metadata (install link, docs link) for a given agent ID from the registry table or overrides.

nodes.name: mmd-routes.ts
nodes.summary: Loads and parses MMD (multi-model dispatch) route configuration files, resolving model IDs, API base URLs, and credential env vars for routed model access.

nodes.name: loadMmdRouteModels
nodes.summary: Reads the MMD routes config file from disk and returns the merged set of model options available via configured routes.

nodes.name: loadMmdRouteLaunchEnv
nodes.summary: Reads the MMD routes config and resolves the launch environment (base URL, API key) for a specific model ID's route.

nodes.name: resolveMmdRoutesFile
nodes.summary: Determines the filesystem path of the MMD routes configuration file from env overrides or default location.

nodes.name: model-registry.ts
nodes.summary: Model registry utilities: merging model option lists, generating cache keys from credentials, normalizing agent model choices, and resolving credential status for providers.

nodes.name: mergeModelOptions
nodes.summary: Merges fetched and suggested model option lists, deduplicating by ID while preserving labels.

nodes.name: modelCatalogCacheKey
nodes.summary: Generates a stable cache key for a model catalog fetch, incorporating provider, base URL, credential fingerprint, and variant.

nodes.name: models.ts
nodes.summary: In-memory model cache: remembers live models discovered during detection, provides lookup for known models, and resolves the effective model for an agent invocation.

nodes.name: resolveModelForAgent
nodes.summary: Resolves the model ID to use for an agent invocation, checking env overrides, user preferences, live-model cache, and fallback defaults.

nodes.name: sanitizeCustomModel
nodes.summary: Validates and sanitizes a custom model ID string, ensuring it matches the allowed character pattern.

nodes.name: executables.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves agent executable paths via environment overrides, PATH scanning, packaged built-in binaries, and Codex app-bundle fallbacks. The canonical resolution logic that detection.ts relies on.

nodes.name: resolveAgentExecutable
nodes.summary: Top-level convenience that resolves an agent executable path, returning just the resolved path or undefined.

nodes.name: inspectAgentExecutableResolution
nodes.summary: Inspects the full executable resolution chain for an agent, trying configured override, PATH, packaged built-in, and Codex app-bundle candidates in priority order.

nodes.name: resolveAmrOpenCodeExecutable
nodes.summary: Resolves the OpenCode companion binary, checking env override, packaged tree, then PATH fallback.

nodes.name: agentSearchDirs
nodes.summary: Returns the ordered list of directories searched when resolving agent binaries on PATH.

nodes.name: resolveOnPath
nodes.summary: Searches resolved PATH directories for a named binary, handling PATHEXT on Windows.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export entry point for the @jini/agent-runtime package, exposing the public API surface including stream handlers, ACP session management, pi-rpc, detection, model registry, and provider modules.

nodes.name: invocation.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the low-level execAgentFile helper that spawns agent child processes with timeout, cwd, and environment configuration for probing and model-listing commands.

nodes.name: execAgentFile
nodes.summary: Executes an agent binary command with configurable timeout, environment, and working directory, wrapping child_process.execFile.

nodes.name: json-event-stream.ts
nodes.summary: Unified NDJSON stream parser that normalizes events from five different agent protocols (OpenCode, Gemini, Kimi, Cursor, Codex) into the canonical runtime event stream, handling text deltas, tool calls, errors, and artifacts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a state-machine pattern with per-protocol handler functions dispatched by kind. Handles artifact deduplication across streaming boundaries.

nodes.name: createJsonEventStreamHandler
nodes.summary: Factory that creates a feed/flush pair for parsing NDJSON lines from a given agent kind into canonical runtime events.

nodes.name: handleCodexEvent
nodes.summary: Handles Codex-protocol NDJSON events: maps text deltas, tool_use/tool_result objects, todo lists, and error/completion signals to canonical events.

nodes.name: handleGeminiEvent
nodes.summary: Handles Gemini-protocol NDJSON events: maps candidates, tool calls, errors, and severity-flagged messages to canonical runtime events with artifact dedup.

nodes.name: handleOpenCodeEvent
nodes.summary: Handles OpenCode-protocol NDJSON events: maps assistant content, tool_use, usage, and error events to canonical runtime events.

nodes.name: handleCursorEvent
nodes.summary: Handles Cursor-protocol NDJSON events: extracts text content from message blocks, reconciles turn replays, and emits text deltas.

nodes.name: anthropic-messages.ts
nodes.summary: Anthropic Messages API provider: constructs requests, streams SSE responses, parses tool-use content blocks, and implements multi-turn tool execution loops with connection guards and role-marker validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the Anthropic streaming protocol with SSE parsing, content_block_delta handling, and tool_use/tool_result message assembly for multi-turn conversations.

nodes.name: runAnthropicToolTurn
nodes.summary: Executes a full Anthropic tool-use turn: sends messages, processes streaming response, invokes tools when requested, and loops until the model stops or a turn limit is reached.

nodes.name: runSingleAnthropicRequest
nodes.summary: Sends a single Anthropic Messages API request, validates the base URL, streams SSE events, parses text and tool_use content blocks, and accumulates tool calls.

nodes.name: azure-chat.ts
nodes.summary: Azure OpenAI Chat provider: builds deployment-specific request URLs with API versioning, handles max_tokens vs max_completion_tokens parameter negotiation, and implements multi-turn tool execution loops.

nodes.name: runAzureToolTurn
nodes.summary: Executes a full Azure OpenAI tool-use turn: sends messages, processes streaming response, invokes tools, and loops until completion or turn limit.

nodes.name: runSingleAzureRequest
nodes.summary: Sends a single Azure OpenAI request with DNS-resolved base URL validation, token parameter fallback, and OpenAI-compatible streaming.

nodes.name: connection-guard.ts
nodes.summary: Network security guards for provider connections: validates base URLs against loopback/private IP ranges, resolves DNS for SSRF prevention, and redacts secrets from error messages.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles IPv4, IPv6, IPv4-mapped-IPv6, and bracketed IP literals. DNS resolution is async with fallback to node:dns/promises.

nodes.name: validateBaseUrl
nodes.summary: Synchronously validates a base URL's protocol and hostname against loopback and private-network blocklists.

nodes.name: validateBaseUrlResolved
nodes.summary: Validates a base URL with DNS resolution to catch SSRF via hostname-to-private-IP resolution, blocking if resolved addresses are loopback or private.

nodes.name: redactSecrets
nodes.summary: Removes Bearer tokens, API key patterns, and exact secret strings from text to prevent credential leakage in error messages.

nodes.name: elevenlabs.ts
nodes.summary: ElevenLabs voice provider: fetches and caches available voice options from the ElevenLabs API, normalizes voice metadata, and handles credential resolution with TTL-based caching.

nodes.name: ElevenLabsCredentialMissingError
nodes.summary: Custom error thrown when ElevenLabs API credentials are not configured, signaling the caller to prompt for credential setup.

nodes.name: listElevenLabsVoiceOptions
nodes.summary: Fetches available voice options from the ElevenLabs API with TTL caching, credential resolution, and response normalization.

nodes.name: opencode-log.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and parses OpenCode agent log files to extract service failure information (HTTP status codes, error messages) for diagnostic reporting when an agent session fails.

nodes.name: readOpenCodeServiceFailure
nodes.summary: Top-level entry that resolves the log directory, reads the latest log tail, and extracts structured service failure information.

nodes.name: extractOpenCodeServiceFailure
nodes.summary: Parses a log tail string to find ERROR lines with HTTP status codes, classifies the failure type, and returns a structured failure descriptor.

nodes.name: readLatestOpenCodeLogTail
nodes.summary: Finds the most recent log file in the OpenCode log directory and reads its tail bytes for error extraction.

nodes.name: paths.ts
nodes.summary: Path expansion utilities: expands tilde (~) in file paths and expands all values in a configured env dict, used throughout the runtime for resolving user-specified paths.

nodes.name: expandHomePath
nodes.summary: Expands tilde-prefixed paths to absolute paths using the system home directory.

nodes.name: expandConfiguredEnv
nodes.summary: Applies tilde expansion to all path-like values in a configured environment dictionary.

nodes.name: pi-models.ts
nodes.summary: Parses the model list output from pi-rpc compatible agents (tab-separated format) into structured model option entries.

nodes.name: parsePiModels
nodes.summary: Parses a pi-rpc models command stdout (tab-separated ID/label lines) into a deduplicated array of model option objects.

nodes.name: prompt-augmenter.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the PromptAugmenter interface and provides a no-op default implementation for augmenting agent prompts before submission.

nodes.name: prompt-budget.ts
nodes.summary: Enforces prompt size limits for agent invocations, handling both Unix argv byte budgets and Windows command-line length constraints (both cmd.exe shim and direct exe quoting).

nodes.name: checkPromptArgvBudget
nodes.summary: Checks whether a composed prompt exceeds the platform's argv byte budget, returning a diagnostic message if so.

nodes.name: checkWindowsCmdShimCommandLineBudget
nodes.summary: Checks whether the quoted command line for a .bat/.cmd shim exceeds the Windows cmd.exe 8191-char limit.

nodes.name: checkWindowsDirectExeCommandLineBudget
nodes.summary: Checks whether the quoted command line for a direct .exe invocation exceeds the Windows CreateProcess 32767-char limit.

nodes.name: prompt-file.ts
nodes.summary: Creates temporary prompt files on disk for agents that accept prompts via file path rather than inline arguments, with automatic cleanup.

nodes.name: preparePromptFileForAgent
nodes.summary: Writes a prompt to a temporary file and returns an object with the file path and a cleanup function to remove it.

nodes.name: aihubmix.ts
nodes.summary: AIHubMix provider utilities: request header construction, model classification (chat/image/video/search), Gemini image generation via AIHubMix endpoint, catalog parsing, and video duration clamping.

nodes.name: parseAIHubMixCatalog
nodes.summary: Parses the AIHubMix model catalog response into a filtered, deduplicated array of model entries, optionally filtering by media generation types.

nodes.name: aihubmixGeminiImageBytes
nodes.summary: Calls the AIHubMix Gemini image generation endpoint, extracts the inline image data from the response, and returns it as a Buffer.

nodes.name: classifyAIHubMixModel
nodes.summary: Classifies an AIHubMix model ID into a category (chat, image, video, search, tts) based on naming conventions.

nodes.name: vibe.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the Vibe agent definition descriptor used by the runtime's agent registry for Vibe-type agents.

nodes.name: detection.ts
nodes.summary: Agent detection pipeline: probes each registered agent definition for availability, version, capabilities, models, and auth status, then assembles the set of usable agents at startup.

nodes.name: detectAgents
nodes.summary: Main entry point that probes all registered agent definitions in parallel, remembers detected live models, and returns the set of available agents.

nodes.name: probe
nodes.summary: Full probe of a single agent: resolves executable, checks version, fetches capabilities and models in parallel, evaluates auth status, and constructs the final detected agent record.

nodes.name: fetchModels
nodes.summary: Fetches available models for an agent by invoking its fetchModels hook or executing its list-models CLI command.

nodes.name: probeVersionAtPath
nodes.summary: Executes the agent binary with version args and parses the version string from stdout to verify the agent is invocable.

nodes.name: stripFns
nodes.summary: Creates a serializable copy of an agent definition by removing function-valued properties that cannot be persisted.

nodes.name: diagnostics.ts
nodes.summary: Builds structured diagnostic messages when agents fail detection: covers executable-not-found, not-invocable, and auth-failure scenarios with actionable fix instructions.

nodes.name: buildExecutableDiagnostic
nodes.summary: Produces a diagnostic object explaining why an agent's executable was not found, including search paths and env-key guidance.

nodes.name: buildNotInvocableDiagnostic
nodes.summary: Produces a diagnostic object explaining that an agent's binary was located but failed to respond to version invocation.

nodes.name: buildAuthDiagnostic
nodes.summary: Produces a diagnostic object explaining that an agent was detected but its auth credentials are missing or expired.

nodes.name: env.ts
nodes.summary: Assembles the spawn environment for each agent process, merging system proxy, configured env, toolchain paths, OpenCode companion resolution, and per-agent hook overlays.

nodes.name: spawnEnvForAgent
nodes.summary: Builds the complete environment variable dict for spawning an agent subprocess, applying proxy settings, path expansion, opencode binary resolution, and per-agent hooks.

nodes.name: google-messages.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the Google Gemini streaming chat completions provider with tool-use loop, SSE decoding, role-marker guard integration, and multi-turn function-calling support.

nodes.name: google.ts
nodes.summary: Provides URL construction utilities for the Google Generative Language API — base URL normalization, model path encoding, and endpoint URL builders for generateContent, streamGenerateContent, and model listing.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export for the providers module, aggregating all LLM provider integrations (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure, Ollama, ElevenLabs, AIHubMix), OAuth utilities, SSE decoding, model catalog, and shared types into a single import surface.

nodes.name: model-catalog.ts
nodes.summary: Lists available models from any supported provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, AIHubMix) by fetching their respective model-listing endpoints, normalizing results, and reporting connectivity status with latency metrics.

nodes.name: oauth-callback-server.ts
nodes.summary: Starts a local HTTP server to receive OAuth authorization code callbacks, validates the state parameter, handles CORS preflight, renders success/error result pages, and auto-closes after timeout or successful code capture.

nodes.name: oauth-credentials.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves a valid OAuth bearer token for API requests by reading stored tokens, checking expiry with configurable skew, and transparently refreshing via PKCE when expired.

nodes.name: oauth-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the OAuth 2.0 PKCE authorization flow lifecycle — begin (generate verifier/challenge/state, build authorize URL), complete (exchange code for token), and refresh (use refresh_token for new access_token). Includes xAI-specific provider configuration constants.

nodes.name: oauth-tokens.ts
nodes.summary: Manages filesystem-backed OAuth token persistence — read, write (with atomic rename and file locking), clear, and expiry-check for stored access/refresh tokens. Uses a simple in-memory write-lock queue to prevent concurrent file corruption.

nodes.name: ollama-chat.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the Ollama streaming chat provider with NDJSON response parsing, tool-call extraction, multi-turn function-calling loop, role-marker guard, and connection validation.

nodes.name: openai-chat.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the OpenAI-compatible streaming chat provider handling SSE decoding, incremental tool-call assembly across delta chunks, role-marker injection detection, automatic max_tokens retry, and the multi-turn tool-execution loop.

nodes.name: pkce.ts
nodes.summary: Low-level OAuth PKCE primitives — code verifier/challenge generation, state nonce, authorize URL construction, code-for-token exchange, refresh-token rotation, and a time-expiring pending-auth cache for correlating callbacks to initiated flows.

nodes.name: sse-decode.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal, tolerant Server-Sent-Events frame decoder for inbound LLM provider streams. Turns raw byte/text chunks into structured {event, data} records per the SSE wire format, shared by both the OpenAI and Google provider turn-runners.

nodes.name: token-params.ts
nodes.summary: Determines the correct max-tokens request parameter for OpenAI-compatible APIs — detects whether a model uses max_completion_tokens vs legacy max_tokens based on model ID patterns (GPT-5, o1/o3/o4), and provides error detection for unsupported parameter responses.

nodes.name: turn-end-guard.ts
nodes.summary: Creates a one-shot guard that ensures each LLM turn emits exactly one end-of-turn event regardless of how many code paths could trigger it — prevents duplicate or missing turn-end emissions across error, timeout, and success paths.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the shared provider-connectivity type contracts — ConnectionTestKind outcome categories, ConnectionTestProtocol wire-protocol family, ProviderModelOption, and ProviderModelsRequest/Response shapes consumed by the model-catalog and connection-guard modules.

nodes.name: qoder-stream.ts
nodes.summary: Parses NDJSON output from the Qoder agent subprocess into normalized runtime events — handles text content, tool calls, errors, and completion signals from the line-delimited JSON stream protocol.

nodes.name: registry.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the built-in agent registry — BASE_AGENT_DEFS for core agents and AGENT_DEFS as the full merged set with user extensions — plus getAgentDef lookup by ID for runtime resolution.

nodes.name: resolution.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves an agent ID to its executable binary path by looking up the agent definition from the registry and delegating to the executables module for filesystem resolution.

nodes.name: role-marker-guard.ts
nodes.summary: Detects and strips fabricated role-marker injection attempts (e.g. fake 'Human:' / 'Assistant:' prefixes) from streaming LLM output, emitting a warning event when a marker is found and sanitizing the text before forwarding to the consumer.

nodes.name: openai.yaml
nodes.summary: Agent interface configuration for the chat-motion-overlay skill — defines display name, short description, default prompt, and implicit-invocation policy for the OpenAI-backed motion overlay generator.

nodes.name: chat-transcript.txt
nodes.summary: Example chat transcript fixture showing a multi-participant conversation format used as input to the chat-motion-overlay skill for video generation.

nodes.name: config-wechat-phone.json
nodes.summary: Example configuration for the chat-motion-overlay skill specifying WeChat container style, iPhone Dynamic Island device frame, preset avatars, hidden nicknames, and MOV delivery format.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Package manifest for the Remotion video template used by the chat-motion-overlay skill — declares Remotion dependencies, render/preview scripts, and TypeScript dev tooling.

nodes.name: remotion.config.ts
nodes.summary: Remotion bundler configuration for the chat-motion-overlay video template — sets up webpack override for the video rendering pipeline.

nodes.name: chatSpec.ts
nodes.summary: Default chat specification constant for the Remotion template — defines timing, scene configuration (WeChat container, iPhone frame, MOV-alpha output), and placeholder participant/message arrays for the motion overlay renderer.

nodes.name: runGoogleToolTurn
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a complete Google Gemini tool-use turn — sends the initial request, executes returned tool calls, appends function responses, and loops until the model produces a final text response or exceeds the turn-end guard limit.

nodes.name: listProviderModels
nodes.summary: Fetches available models from a provider's model-listing endpoint with timeout/abort handling, caching by URL, error categorization (auth failure, rate limit, network), and result normalization into a uniform ProviderModelsResponse.

nodes.name: startOAuthCallbackListener
nodes.summary: Starts a local HTTP server bound to a specified port, handles the OAuth redirect callback with state validation and CORS, delivers the authorization code or error to the provided callback, and auto-stops after a configurable timeout.

nodes.name: resolveOAuthBearer
nodes.summary: Resolves a valid bearer token for API authentication — reads the stored token, checks expiry with clock skew tolerance, and automatically refreshes via PKCE refresh_token flow when the access_token has expired.

nodes.name: beginOAuthPkce
nodes.summary: Initiates an OAuth PKCE flow — generates code verifier, challenge, and state nonce, builds the authorization URL, stores the pending auth in the cache, and returns the URL for the user to open.

nodes.name: completeOAuthPkce
nodes.summary: Completes an OAuth PKCE flow by consuming the pending auth from cache, validating the state, and exchanging the authorization code for access and refresh tokens.

nodes.name: refreshOAuthPkceToken
nodes.summary: Refreshes an expired OAuth access token using the stored refresh token and the provider's token endpoint.

nodes.name: runOllamaToolTurn
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a complete Ollama tool-use turn — sends the chat request, parses NDJSON streaming response for tool calls, executes tools, appends results as tool-role messages, and loops until final text or turn-end.

nodes.name: runOpenAiCompatibleRequest
nodes.summary: Executes a single streaming request against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — handles SSE decoding, incremental tool-call delta assembly, role-marker guard filtering, max_tokens retry on unsupported-parameter errors, and structured event emission.

nodes.name: runOpenAiToolTurn
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a complete OpenAI-compatible tool-use turn — sends the initial request, executes returned tool calls, appends tool-result messages, and loops until the model emits final text or the turn-end guard fires.

nodes.name: PendingAuthCache
nodes.summary: Time-expiring in-memory cache for pending OAuth authorization flows. Stores verifier/challenge/state tuples keyed by state nonce, auto-sweeps expired entries, and provides atomic consume semantics for one-time state validation.

nodes.name: buildAuthorizeUrl
nodes.summary: Constructs the OAuth authorization URL with all required PKCE parameters — client_id, redirect_uri, response_type, scope, state, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method.

nodes.name: exchangeCodeForToken
nodes.summary: Exchanges an OAuth authorization code for access and refresh tokens by posting the code, verifier, redirect_uri, and client credentials to the token endpoint.

nodes.name: refreshAccessToken
nodes.summary: Refreshes an expired OAuth access token by posting the refresh_token and client credentials to the token endpoint.

nodes.name: decodeSseStream
nodes.summary: Async generator that decodes an inbound byte/text stream into SSE records ({event, data} pairs) per the Server-Sent-Events wire format, handling both CR+LF and LF line endings, comment filtering, and trailing unterminated record flushing.

nodes.name: createTurnEndGuard
nodes.summary: Creates a one-shot guard ensuring exactly one turn-end event is emitted — the returned emitEnd function fires the end event on first call and no-ops on subsequent calls, with a hasEnded() query for loop control.

nodes.name: createRoleMarkerGuard
nodes.summary: Creates a streaming text filter that buffers incoming LLM text to detect fabricated role-marker injection patterns (fake 'Human:'/'Assistant:' prefixes), strips matched markers, emits a warning event on detection, and releases safe text incrementally.

nodes.name: createQoderStreamHandler
nodes.summary: Creates a line-buffered NDJSON stream handler for Qoder subprocess output — parses each JSON line into normalized runtime events (text deltas, tool calls, errors, completion) and handles malformed lines gracefully.

nodes.name: resolveAgentBin
nodes.summary: Resolves an agent ID to its executable binary path by fetching the definition from the registry and delegating to resolveAgentExecutable for filesystem lookup.

nodes.name: avatarLibrary.tsx
nodes.summary: Provides avatar image resolution and rendering for chat overlay participants, mapping participant names to static file avatar sources.

nodes.name: AvatarImage
nodes.summary: React component that renders a circular avatar image with configurable size and border styling.

nodes.name: BubbleScene.tsx
nodes.summary: Core Remotion scene component that renders animated chat bubbles with text wrapping, avatar placement, spring animations, and scroll-based viewport management.

nodes.name: measureTextWidth
nodes.summary: Measures text width using canvas API with fallback to character-width estimation for environments without DOM.

nodes.name: wrapMessageText
nodes.summary: Word-wraps message text into lines that fit within a maximum pixel width, handling paragraph breaks.

nodes.name: Bubble
nodes.summary: Renders a single animated chat bubble with spring entrance animation, avatar, timestamp, and dynamically sized text content.

nodes.name: BubbleScene
nodes.summary: Top-level scene that orchestrates all chat bubbles with scroll interpolation, participant headers, and sequential message appearance.

nodes.name: ChatMotionOverlay.tsx
nodes.summary: Composition wrapper that combines the DeviceFrame and BubbleScene into the final chat motion overlay Remotion composition.

nodes.name: ChatMotionOverlay
nodes.summary: Wraps BubbleScene inside a DeviceFrame to produce the final rendered chat overlay composition.

nodes.name: DeviceFrame.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders a mobile device frame (phone bezel with notch and status bar) as a visual wrapper for overlay content.

nodes.name: designMdModuleSlice
nodes.summary: Locates and extracts a module-specific section from a design markdown document by matching heading keywords, returning the slice boundaries and content or synthesizing a default.

nodes.name: replaceDesignMdModule
nodes.summary: Replaces a module section within a design markdown document body, normalizing the draft and reassembling surrounding content.

nodes.name: dom-subscriptions.ts
nodes.summary: Provides subscribe-and-unsubscribe helper functions for common DOM patterns: outside-click/escape dismissal, window events, visibility changes, timers, and external URL opening.

nodes.name: subscribeOutsideClickOrEscape
nodes.summary: Subscribes to document-level pointerdown and keydown events to detect clicks outside a container ref or Escape key presses, returning an unsubscribe function.

nodes.name: subscribeVisibleFocusOrVisibilityChange
nodes.summary: Subscribes to window focus and document visibilitychange events, invoking a callback only when the document becomes visible. Returns an unsubscribe function.

nodes.name: file-system-errors.ts
nodes.summary: Defines structured file-system read error creation and type-guard utilities, wrapping native errors with a recognizable marker message for downstream handling.

nodes.name: errorSummary
nodes.summary: Extracts a human-readable summary string from an unknown error by checking for Error instances, objects with message property, or stringifying the value.

nodes.name: file-transfer.ts
nodes.summary: Handles file extraction from clipboard paste and drag-and-drop events, including recursive directory reading via the File System Access API and WebKit fallbacks.

nodes.name: filesFromClipboardData
nodes.summary: Extracts files from a ClipboardEvent's DataTransfer, handling both the files list and items list to normalize pasted files.

nodes.name: filesFromDataTransfer
nodes.summary: Extracts files from a drag-and-drop DataTransfer object, resolving directory entries recursively via webkitGetAsEntry and falling back to flat file lists.

nodes.name: filesFromFileSystemEntry
nodes.summary: Recursively reads files from a FileSystemEntry, handling both file entries and directory entries by batching reader results.

nodes.name: ime-composing.ts
nodes.summary: Detects whether a keyboard event is part of an IME composition sequence, guarding against premature keystroke handling during CJK or multi-key input.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export file aggregating all public utilities from the utils directory: file errors, IME detection, notifications/sounds, platform detection, scroll helpers, UUID generation, and visual stability.

nodes.name: localized-url.ts
nodes.summary: Builds a locale-aware URL by injecting a locale prefix into a configurable base URL template, supporting multi-language documentation links.

nodes.name: markdown-scroll-sync.ts
nodes.summary: Implements bidirectional scroll synchronization between a markdown source textarea and its rendered preview pane by measuring block-level offsets via a mirror DOM element and mapping scroll positions through paired anchor points.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a hidden mirror DOM element to measure character offsets in the textarea, matching them to rendered preview elements via block-level correspondences.

nodes.name: extractMarkdownBlockLines
nodes.summary: Parses markdown text using micromark with GFM extensions to identify top-level block boundaries (headings, paragraphs, code blocks, lists) and returns their starting line numbers.

nodes.name: measureEditorBlockOffsets
nodes.summary: Measures pixel offsets of markdown blocks within a textarea by constructing a hidden mirror element with matching styles, inserting markers at block boundaries, and reading their offsetTop values.

nodes.name: measurePreviewBlockOffsets
nodes.summary: Measures pixel offsets of rendered preview blocks by querying direct children of an article element and computing their top positions relative to the preview pane.

nodes.name: buildScrollAnchors
nodes.summary: Constructs normalized scroll anchor points from raw block offsets, mapping each block's position to a 0-1 ratio relative to total scroll height.

nodes.name: mapScrollPosition
nodes.summary: Maps a scroll position from source anchor coordinates to target anchor coordinates using linear interpolation between the nearest bounding anchor pair.

nodes.name: notifications.ts
nodes.summary: Provides browser notification and sound feedback utilities: Web Audio API tone synthesis for success/failure sounds, Notification API permission management, and service-worker or constructor-based desktop notifications.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Web Audio API oscillators and biquad filters for synthesized notification sounds rather than audio file playback.

nodes.name: getCtx
nodes.summary: Lazily creates or resumes a shared AudioContext singleton, returning null when the Web Audio API is unavailable.

nodes.name: playTones
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a sequence of tones using Web Audio oscillators with gain envelopes and optional biquad filters, scheduling start/stop times for each note.

nodes.name: playSound
nodes.summary: Plays a registered notification sound by ID, looking up the sound definition and invoking its player function with the shared AudioContext.

nodes.name: requestNotificationPermission
nodes.summary: Requests browser notification permission from the user, returning the resulting permission state or 'denied' if the API is unavailable.

nodes.name: showCompletionNotification
nodes.summary: Dispatches a desktop completion notification via service worker when available, falling back to the Notification constructor for direct display.

nodes.name: showViaConstructor
nodes.summary: Creates a native Notification via the constructor, managing click focus restoration, auto-close timeouts, and tracking active notifications to prevent duplicates.

nodes.name: platform.ts
nodes.summary: Exports a single platform detection function that identifies macOS and iOS devices via user-agent string matching.

nodes.name: polygon-selection.ts
nodes.summary: Implements 2D computational geometry primitives for lasso/polygon selection: closed-loop detection, point-in-polygon ray casting, line-line intersection, and rect-vs-polygon hit testing.

nodes.name: pointInPolygon
nodes.summary: Determines whether a 2D point lies inside a polygon using the ray-casting algorithm, counting edge crossings to determine interior/exterior status.

nodes.name: pathIntersectsRect
nodes.summary: Tests whether a polyline path intersects a given rectangle by checking each path segment against all four rectangle edges.

nodes.name: lassoSelectionHitsRect
nodes.summary: Determines if a lasso selection (open path or closed polygon) hits a target rectangle by combining path intersection, center containment, and corner containment checks.

nodes.name: scroll-tabs-with-wheel.ts
nodes.summary: Converts vertical mouse wheel events into horizontal scroll on a tab bar element, handling deltaMode normalization for line and page scroll units.

nodes.name: scrollTabsWithWheel
nodes.summary: Intercepts a wheel event on a horizontal tab bar, converting vertical delta to horizontal scrollLeft when the vertical component dominates.

nodes.name: smooth-scroll-to-top.ts
nodes.summary: Implements a custom smooth-scroll-to-top animation using a cubic bezier easing curve and requestAnimationFrame, respecting reduced-motion preferences and cancelling on user interaction.

nodes.name: unitBezier
nodes.summary: Returns an easing function implementing a cubic bezier curve solver using Newton-Raphson iteration to find t for a given x, then evaluating the corresponding y.

nodes.name: smoothScrollToTop
nodes.summary: Animates a container's scroll to the top using bezier easing over requestAnimationFrame, deduplicating concurrent animations and cancelling on user wheel or touch events.

nodes.name: sse.ts
nodes.summary: Parses Server-Sent Events (SSE) frames into structured objects with event type, data (optionally JSON-parsed), id, retry, and comment fields.

nodes.name: parseSseFrame
nodes.summary: Parses a raw SSE frame string into a structured SseEvent object, handling event, data, id, retry, and comment lines with optional JSON data parsing.

nodes.name: timezone.ts
nodes.summary: Provides timezone utilities for detecting the user's local timezone via Intl API, listing supported IANA timezones, and formatting timezone labels for display.

nodes.name: detectLocalTimezone
nodes.summary: Detects the user's local IANA timezone string using the Intl.DateTimeFormat API, falling back to UTC on failure.

nodes.name: listSupportedTimezones
nodes.summary: Returns a list of IANA timezone identifiers supported by the runtime, using Intl.supportedValuesOf when available with a built-in fallback.

nodes.name: uuid.ts
nodes.summary: Generates RFC 4122 v4 UUIDs using a multi-tier strategy: native crypto.randomUUID, crypto.getRandomValues with manual formatting, or Math.random fallback for legacy environments.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a tiered fallback chain to maximize browser and Node.js compatibility without external dependencies.

nodes.name: randomUUID
nodes.summary: Generates a v4 UUID string with three fallback implementations: native crypto.randomUUID, getRandomValues with manual hex formatting, and a Math.random-based last resort.

nodes.name: visual-stability.ts
nodes.summary: Checks localStorage for a visual-stability flag used to suppress layout-shifting animations or transitions for accessibility or testing purposes.

nodes.name: isVisualStabilityMode
nodes.summary: Reads a localStorage key to determine whether visual stability mode is active, suppressing animations and transitions for accessibility.

nodes.name: zip.ts
nodes.summary: Pure-TypeScript ZIP archive builder that creates uncompressed ZIP files in-memory from an array of named byte entries, implementing the ZIP local/central/end-of-central-directory format directly via DataView.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements ZIP file format at the byte level using Uint8Array and DataView for cross-platform in-browser archive creation without compression libraries.

nodes.name: buildZip
nodes.summary: Builds an uncompressed ZIP archive as a Uint8Array from an array of named entries, constructing local file headers, central directory entries, and end-of-central-directory record.

nodes.name: crc32
nodes.summary: Computes CRC-32 checksum for a byte array using a precomputed lookup table, required for ZIP file integrity.

nodes.name: dosTime
nodes.summary: Converts a JavaScript Date into DOS time and date format (two 16-bit values) as required by the ZIP file specification.

nodes.name: vitest-chat-entry.ts
nodes.summary: Test entry point barrel that re-exports chat-related UI components (AgentIcon, RemixIcon, WorkingDirPicker) and the useFileDropTarget hook for test environment use.

nodes.name: vitest-env.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient type declaration file that provides Vitest global type references for the test environment.

nodes.name: vitest-jest-dom.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient type declaration file that provides jest-dom matcher types for Vitest, enabling DOM assertion type-checking in tests.

nodes.name: AgentExecutor
nodes.summary: Kernel port for driving a coding-agent subprocess through one run — `run()` wires @jini/agent-runtime stream parsers into RunLifecycle so agent output becomes canonical run events.

nodes.name: ArtifactStore
nodes.summary: Kernel port for a store of named artifacts with validated manifests (create/get/list). A reference in-memory implementation ships alongside it; a durable adapter implements the same interface.

nodes.name: AuthProvider
nodes.summary: Connector port for pluggable authentication: sign-up, sign-in, sign-out, and session verification, so route packs never bind to one auth backend.

nodes.name: CapabilityRegistry
nodes.summary: Registry port for media capabilities — register/get/all over provider-contributed capability descriptors.

nodes.name: DbProvider
nodes.summary: Connector port for a pluggable database backend: insert/get/update/delete plus query, keeping route packs independent of any concrete store.

nodes.name: EventLog
nodes.summary: Kernel port for a replayable, ordered, per-run event log (append/replay/listRunIds/drop). `createInMemoryEventLog` is the reference implementation; @jini/sqlite is the durable adapter.

nodes.name: MediaPolicy
nodes.summary: Host-injected policy port evaluated before media generation. @jini/media never calls it itself — a caller evaluates a target and honors a non-null denial.

nodes.name: MediaTaskStore
nodes.summary: Port for a replayable, ownerRef-scoped store of async media-generation tasks, including boot-time reconciliation of interrupted work.

nodes.name: PaymentsProvider
nodes.summary: Connector port for a pluggable payments backend: charge, retrieve a charge, and refund.

nodes.name: ProtocolHandlerPort
nodes.summary: Desktop-host port for registering a custom URL-scheme fetch proxy inside the shell process.

nodes.name: RealtimeProvider
nodes.summary: Connector port for pluggable realtime publish/subscribe messaging.

nodes.name: RenderService
nodes.summary: Host-process rendering port (renderToPdf/capture/exportArtifact). Bound via the registry and called directly by a daemon or export route — deliberately NOT reachable through the renderer bridge.

nodes.name: RunLifecycle
nodes.summary: The kernel run state machine port: start/emit/cancel/finish/resume/stream/rehydrate keyed on an opaque contextRef, backed by an injected EventLog, with idempotent start and reconnect-safe replay.

nodes.name: ShellPort
nodes.summary: Desktop-host port for local-machine shell capabilities: open an external URL or path, test directory existence, list recent folders, and raise the native folder dialog.

nodes.name: SidecarLauncherPort
nodes.summary: Desktop-host port for spawning and supervising a sidecar child process, polling a caller-supplied readiness probe with graceful-shutdown fallback.

nodes.name: SingleInstanceLockPort
nodes.summary: Desktop-host port for the single-instance lock, bound to one app instance at construction like WindowLifecyclePort and ProtocolHandlerPort.

nodes.name: StorageProvider
nodes.summary: Connector port for pluggable object storage: put/get/delete/list.

nodes.name: ToolExecutor
nodes.summary: The sole tool-invocation boundary: authorize -> confirm -> execute -> audit, with resumable confirmation, timeout, cancellation, and output truncation. Registered handlers are reachable ONLY through this port — routes and agents hold descriptors, never the handler.

nodes.name: ToolRegistry
nodes.summary: The public tool registration/enumeration surface (register/has/list). Exposes descriptors only — handlers and policies are never retrievable through it, which is what forces ToolExecutor to be the single invocation path.

nodes.name: WindowLifecyclePort
nodes.summary: Desktop-host port for main-window creation, retrieval, and reveal.

nodes.name: ConnectorCredentialStore
nodes.summary: Port for storing and retrieving per-provider connector credentials (get/set/delete/deleteByProvider).

nodes.name: DeployTarget
nodes.summary: The port every deploy provider implements (id/publish/checkReachability). Bound many-to-one against the DeployTarget token so Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, and later targets all register against one capability.

nodes.name: PtyProcess
nodes.summary: A single running PTY child process (onData/onExit/write/resize/kill), abstracted from however the caller’s backend spawns it.

nodes.name: RegistryBackend
nodes.summary: The contract every concrete registry source implements — a GitHub-hosted index, HTTP endpoint, local directory, or DB: list/search/resolve/manifest/doctor plus optional publish/yank.

nodes.name: RoutinePersistence
nodes.summary: Synchronous storage port the routine scheduler is injected with (list/insertRun/updateRun/getLatestRun). Deliberately synchronous, unlike this repo’s usual async-port convention.

nodes.name: TerminalSseSink
nodes.summary: A minimal push sink (send/end) that a transport adapts its live connection to, e.g. SSE.

nodes.name: CTX-global-assistant-chat-scope-2026-07-12.md
nodes.summary: Swarm-consensus context packet (2026-07-12) framing the delivery path and first-PR scope for a workspace-level global assistant chat that can both drive the desktop app’s UI and perform durable product actions. States the question and option space without carrying any participant’s answer.

nodes.name: CTX-jini-architecture-debate-2026-07-19.md
nodes.summary: Swarm-consensus context packet (2026-07-19) asking whether structural/architectural decisions should be reconsidered mid-port — while the extraction is ~44% complete and still malleable — rather than after another ~93K lines land on the current shape.

nodes.name: CTX-run-chat-orchestration-2026-07-21-round1-prompt.md
nodes.summary: Round-1 blind debate prompt for the run/chat orchestration question: five capability gaps (run→agent wiring, prompt/skill/memory composition, multi-turn tool loop, retry classification, session resume) plus prompt-injection and observability concerns, with three options to evaluate on equal footing.

nodes.name: CTX-run-chat-orchestration-2026-07-21.md
nodes.summary: Swarm-consensus context packet (2026-07-21) defining what Jini’s run/chat orchestration layer should look like, given four materially different downstream consumers and the kernel’s locked product-neutral vocabulary (no Project/Conversation nouns, one shared ToolExecutor gate).

nodes.name: CTX-ui-audit-2026-07-22.md
nodes.summary: Swarm-debate context packet (2026-07-22) for the @jini/ui architectural and coverage audit — 100% statement/branch/function/line coverage across components, hooks, and features, plus component modularity and hook dependency-injection patterns.

layers.name: Protocol Layer
layers.description: The pure wire vocabulary (@jini/protocol) that every other package projects from -- event/message DTOs and transport-agnostic types with zero dependencies of its own.

layers.name: Core Layer
layers.description: The engine kernel (@jini/core): the tool registry and dependency-injection tokens that the daemon and transports build on top of.

layers.name: Daemon Layer
layers.description: The run lifecycle engine (@jini/daemon): RunLifecycle, EventLog, ToolExecutor, and AgentExecutor that durably drive and stream agent runs.

layers.name: Transport Layer
layers.description: The protocol-facing transports (http, cli, mcp, sidecar) that expose the daemon over HTTP, terminal, MCP, and sidecar-process channels.

layers.name: Platform Adapters
layers.description: Host and storage adapters (sqlite, platform, desktop-host) that bind the engine to a concrete OS, filesystem, and persistence backend.

layers.name: Agent Runtime Layer
layers.description: Coding-agent process management (@jini/agent-runtime): the ACP+pi-rpc agent-protocol transport, provider detection/registry/defs, streaming output parsers for each agent CLI, and bundled agent skills.

layers.name: Capability & Provider Layer
layers.description: Tool- and resource-capability packages (media, memory, artifacts, registry, deploy, capability-providers, composio, metatool, diagnostics, node-host) that give agents things to call and consume beyond the core run loop.

layers.name: UI Layer
layers.description: The chat and rendering front-end (ui, chat-react, renderers-react, chat-core, agui) -- generic, non-product-branded components, chat surfaces, and streaming render adapters consumed by host apps.

layers.name: Documentation Layer
layers.description: Every document node in the indexed scope: package source-maps and READMEs, ADS-memory governance/knowledge/reports/specs, foundry/docs architecture and port-planning material, and the two root design docs.

layers.name: Configuration Layer
layers.description: Every config node in the indexed scope: package.json/tsconfig-style manifests and other build/tooling configuration across all packages and foundry/docs.

tour.title: Project Overview & Locked Architecture
tour.description: Jini is a reusable, product-neutral engine for running coding agents, exposing tools and providers, and streaming durable run events over HTTP, CLI, MCP, and sidecar transports, extracted from a product called Open Design. START-HERE.md is the mandatory session entry point summarizing what Jini is and confirming the architecture is locked; extraction-plan.md is the authority document defining the kernel nouns, composition contracts, the package set, and the neutrality guardrails every later package must honor. Together they set the map this tour follows: protocol, then core, then daemon, then transports and adapters, then the UI layer.

tour.title: The Protocol Layer: Wire Vocabulary
tour.description: @jini/protocol is the foundation every other package projects from: pure, dependency-free types with no imports of its own. events.ts defines the discriminated-union event type and RUN_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant that every run event on the wire conforms to; run.ts defines the canonical RUN_STATES/TERMINAL_RUN_STATES state machine; errors.ts defines the shared error-code vocabulary used across the engine. index.ts barrels all of this into the single public surface that core, the daemon, and every transport import.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions (events.ts's tagged union on a `type` field) let consumers switch on that field and get compiler-checked exhaustiveness -- the same pattern repeats for every event flowing across the transports covered later in this tour.

tour.title: The Core Kernel: DI Tokens & Tool Registry
tour.description: @jini/core sits directly on protocol and provides the kernel machinery everything else composes with: bindings.ts implements a lightweight dependency-injection container resolving single- and multi-value tokens; tool-registry.ts manages tool definitions by ID with principal-scoped resolution; pack.ts defines the Pack abstraction, a typed bundle of DI tokens plus a factory function. core's own daemon.ts is the daemon *factory* that assembles a service container from a Pack and bindings -- not to be confused with the @jini/daemon package explored next.
tour.languageLesson: Typed DI tokens (a `Token<T>` wrapper) let `Bindings.resolve()` return a compile-time-correct type without runtime reflection -- a common way to keep dependency injection type-safe in TypeScript.

tour.title: The Daemon: Run Lifecycle, Event Log & Tool Execution
tour.description: Built on core's DI container, @jini/daemon is the run-lifecycle engine at the heart of the system. run-lifecycle.ts implements the RunLifecycle state machine (start/emit/finish/cancel/resume) using the RUN_STATES vocabulary from Step 2; event-log.ts is the in-memory append/replay log every run's events pass through; tool-executor.ts is described as "the sole tool-invocation boundary," enforcing policy gating, confirmation, timeouts, and an audit trail so handlers are unreachable except through it; agent-executor.ts is "the sole agent-execution boundary," spawning child processes and wiring their stdio/ACP/pi-rpc lifecycle. These four modules are the daemon's real substance -- every package after this one exists to expose or support them.

tour.title: Transports: Exposing the Daemon
tour.description: With the daemon able to run agents and execute tools, the transport packages expose that capability over different channels: http/index.ts barrels route handlers, middleware, adapters, and SSE utilities for HTTP streaming; cli/index.ts surfaces the terminal command surface (flags, daemon-url, HTTP client, prompts); mcp/index.ts exposes the daemon as an MCP server and client with tool/resource protocol handlers; sidecar/index.ts exposes contract descriptors and IPC types for out-of-process integration. Each transport is a thin adapter over the same RunLifecycle/EventLog/ToolExecutor spine from Step 4 -- none of them re-implement run semantics.
tour.languageLesson: Barrel files (an `index.ts` that only re-exports sibling modules) give each package one clean public entry point, so consumers write `import { X } from '@jini/http'` instead of reaching into internal file paths.

tour.title: Platform Adapters: Storage & Host Bindings
tour.description: Where transports expose the daemon outward, the adapter packages bind it downward to a concrete host. sqlite/index.ts is "the default durable store adapter behind @jini/daemon's ports," giving the in-memory EventLog from Step 4 real persistence; platform/index.ts aggregates OS-level utilities such as process management, filesystem operations, and proxy resolution; desktop-host/index.ts re-exports ports and adapters for both Electron and Tauri backends, letting the same daemon run inside a desktop shell. This is the layer that turns the abstract Pack/Bindings composition from Step 3 into a process running on a real machine.

tour.title: Agent Runtime: Driving Coding-Agent Processes
tour.description: @jini/agent-runtime is what Step 4's agent-executor.ts actually spawns and talks to. Its top-level index.ts barrels the ACP+pi-rpc transport, provider detection, and model registry; providers/index.ts aggregates every LLM provider integration (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure, Ollama, and more) behind one import surface; the agent-protocol README documents the transport adapters and the "product-neutral seams" added so this piece works for any consumer, not only Open Design. At over 140 files it is the largest single package outside the UI layer, reflecting how much surface area "run an arbitrary coding-agent CLI and stream its output" actually requires.

tour.title: Capability & Provider Layer: Tools Agents Can Call
tour.description: Beyond running agents, the engine gives them things to call. composio.ts is "the sole provider-level boundary between the engine and the Composio API," managing OAuth flows, catalog discovery, and credentialed tool execution; static-backend.ts is the abstract base for the package registry's backends, providing list/search/resolve/manifest/doctor operations over a static manifest that the Database and GitHub backends both extend. Together with sibling packages like media, memory, artifacts, and deploy, this is where the policy-gated calls enforced by Step 4's tool-executor.ts actually land.

tour.title: The UI Layer: Chat Surface & Rendering
tour.description: On the client side, five packages form the UI layer. chat-core defines transport-agnostic chat primitives (events, messages, tools, todos); chat-react wraps them in React hooks and components (useRunStream, useConversation, Composer, MessageList); renderers-react turns streamed artifacts into rendered output (shiki highlighting, sandboxed srcdoc, an annotation canvas); agui encodes agent-to-UI events for consumers; and ui/index.ts is the broadest barrel of all, re-exporting every generic, non-product-branded feature and component. Everything here ultimately consumes the same protocol events from Step 2 that the transports in Step 5 carried across the wire.

tour.title: A UI Feature in Depth: i18n & Shared Components
tour.description: To see the UI layer's internal shape concretely, look at its two most depended-upon files in the entire codebase. features/i18n/index.ts, with 88 incoming references, exposes the Locale/TranslationDict types, locale-detection ports, and the I18nProvider/useI18n/useT hooks that nearly every other feature imports for translated strings. Icon.tsx, with 47 incoming references, is a single inline-SVG icon library rendering over 100 named icons through one switch-case component. Their outsized fan-in is exactly why they were chosen for this step -- understanding them explains a large share of how the rest of Step 9's UI package is wired together.

tour.title: Configuration & Package Metadata
tour.description: packages/README.md documents the workspace-level convention every package in this tour follows: a canonical `jini` field in package.json declaring domain/kind/runtime/admission metadata, enforced by `pnpm guard`. core/package.json and daemon/package.json are two concrete instances of that manifest, turning the dependency direction this tour has followed -- core has no dependency on daemon, daemon depends on core -- into an enforceable, machine-checked contract rather than just a convention.

tour.title: Governance & Decision Records
tour.description: ADS-memory is the project's durable memory, separate from the engine code but tracking every decision made about it. The governance README indexes contracts, ADRs, and computational controls that constrain how the pipeline itself may change the code; the reports README indexes retained AI Dev Shop artifacts -- architecture decisions, reviews, test certifications -- with a pointer to the live test-gap ledger. Where Step 1's START-HERE.md and extraction-plan.md set the locked architecture, this is where the ongoing record of compliance with it lives.

tour.title: Shipping the Engine: CI/CD & Quality Plan
tour.description: The tour closes with ci-cd-plan.md, one of the two root design docs, which defines how everything covered so far actually gets tested and shipped: GitHub Actions structure separating fast and full CI workflows, a unit/boundary/concurrency/integration test strategy, a flaky-test policy, an autonomous-quality system with authority separation, PR scope rules, and a phased rollout for CD artifact promotion. It is the capstone that turns the protocol-to-UI architecture from this tour into a system that can keep changing safely over time.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows commonly split fast feedback (a lightweight job on every push) from a fuller gated suite before merge -- keeping PR iteration quick without sacrificing coverage before release.
